text: GitHub cache scoping: a pull_request run restores caches from its own pull request's scope (refs/pull/N/merge) and the base branch, not from a plain push run on the head branch. So when verification starts, open (or update) the job's pull request with the candidate as its head through the same host seam land uses, rather than only pushing the branch, so the CI run that saves the fingerprint entry is a pull_request run in that pull request's scope, and the landing push (a synchronize event) reuses it. Opening the pull request early must not merge anything: the merge stays with athena land after verification passes. A failure to open or update it is non-fatal.
